newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Centennial lifts bid for Allied.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Centennial lifts bid for Allied.

text.p: Centennial Coal Co Ltd said on Tuesday it had lifted its takeover bid for Allied Queensland Coalfields Ltd to 75 cents per share from 60 cents per share previously.
The new offer matches that made last Friday by Marsford Investments Pte Ltd, a Singapore unit of Hong Kong's Consolidated Electric Power Asia Ltd.

Local brokers had speculated that a bidding war would soon begin for Allied Queensland, a steaming coal miner with operations based in the Surat Basin. Most of its output goes to domestic power stations but it has a growing proportion of Asian sales, with future growth reliant on transport infrastructure improvements between the mines and port facilities.
Clyde Petroleum Plc owns 43.4 percent of Allied Queensland by virtue of its takeover of Crusader Ltd this year.
Clyde has said it would sell to Marsford in the absence of a higher offer, but has also said it would leave its sale options open depending on how the takeover offers progressed.
Allied Queensland shares ended two cents higher at a 12 month high of 76 cents, giving the company a market capitalisation of A$20.99 million.

Crusader, which already has a 10 percent stake, said in its revised offer announcement that it had dropped a previous condition that Crusader vary the terms of a loan to Allied Queensland by foregoing interest payments.
